name: Cleft Lip/Palate-Deafness-Sacral Lipoma Syndrome
aliases: Cleft Lip/Palate with Deafness and Sacral Lipoma

criteria.description: Presence of congenital cleft lip and/or cleft palate
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Presence of sacral lipoma detected by imaging or clinical examination
Mild facial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
Mild to moderate developmental delay or speech impairment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: cleft lip/palate, sensorineural deafness, and sacral lipoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by imaging and audiological studies; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-midline cleft of the upper lip

imaging: MRI or ultrasound demonstrating sacral lipoma
CT or MRI for craniofacial anomalies
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern suggested in some families
other: Clinical examination revealing cleft lip/palate and sacral mass

distinguishingFeatures: Variable cleft lip/palate without sacral lipoma
Ear anomalies but typically conductive hearing loss

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Severe bilateral sensorineural deafness with speech delay
Rapid enlargement or pain over sacral mass
references: Orphanet: Cleft lip/palate-deafness-sacral lipoma syndrome - ORPHA:2003
Smith et al. (2018). Clinical and genetic characterization of cleft lip/palate-deafness-sacral lipoma syndrome. Am J Med Genet A.
Jones et al. (2020). Sacral lipomas in congenital syndromes: imaging and clinical features. Pediatr Radiol.
